author: sonnet
label: pilot-01
changes: Step 1 and the overview now say the click handler must handle both a CSV body and a 202 JSON (and 429); step 3 states the stale-row_count fallback runs step 4 in the same request and returns the 202, with nothing partial ever sent.
Added a per-server cap of 8 concurrent small-path exports (about 40 MB) with a 429 beyond that, and justified the memory use.

Consolidated recovery into one place in step 4: the never-enqueued claim uses a conditional updated_at update so only one click enqueues, and abandonment is judged by a worker heartbeat rather than a flat 2-hour age.

Added a single table of allowed status transitions, all conditional updates. The worker's claim only moves queued to running, so retries cannot clobber queued, and the heartbeat check lets a live job stop if its row was marked failed. The check is repeated just before complete_multipart.
Made the Download button in step 8 explicitly required, and step 6 says that if the email never succeeds, the user gets the file from the page.

Gave the time budget an owner (the engineer building step 5, benchmark first) and a fallback (resumable multipart with checkpoints, or a longer timeout). Stale thresholds now account for queue wait, with the 6-hour backlog assumption flagged as an open question.

Stated one permission stance (checked at click, job start and page download; not rechecked at completion; the emailed link lasts 24 hours as the brief requires) and removed it from the open questions.

Simplified the document. It now has 9 steps, with the path decision merged into step 2 and the click response merged into step 4. The separate Terms section is folded into a short paragraph. The 'nothing visible until complete_multipart' point is no longer repeated. The row_count source is resolved as a stated assumption instead of an open question inside step 2. The one-per-report note is shortened to a page message.

Showed the memory arithmetic (8 MB buffer + about 2.3 MB page + about 2.3 MB encoded, about 13 MB, under 50 MB with overhead), changed the test threshold to match, and spelled out the 4,000 versus 400 round trips (2M rows at 500 versus 5,000 per page).

Point 1: kept both paths (the brief fixes them) and added a note explaining why; simplified the small path by capping the read at 10,001 rows and clarifying the per-server counter and that the 429 can only occur before reading starts, never from the stale-count fallback.

Point 2: replaced the 'two kinds' text with a three-row recovery table (enqueue raises, never enqueued, abandoned) and spelled out what happens after the claim winner enqueues (saves job_id, which stops further claims) and if the winner's enqueue fails or the winner dies.

Point 3: replaced the 45-minute threshold with 15 minutes and derived it from the heartbeat gap plus the 300 s backoff; reduced the queued-with-job_id threshold from 6 hours to 2 hours, stated it as an assumption, explained what a slow-but-live job does, and kept it as open question 1.

Point 4: rewrote step 5.1 as an explicit case list (not found, done, failed, claim). Added an `attempt` column and claim rule so only one worker owns an attempt and a higher attempt takes over; heartbeat and done writes require the owning attempt. Step 6 now has a clear 6.1 and 6.2, and 5.1 jumps to 6.2.

Point 5: documented the publish-to-done window as a known, millisecond-wide gap, explained why a click cannot race into it (heartbeat refreshed just before publish), and said what happens if it ever did (done update changes 0 rows, no email, orphan object expires, never linked).

Point 6: made the heartbeat interval a guarantee by adding 30-second timeouts to every page query and part upload and a heartbeat after each page and each part, bounding the gap to about 60 s; removed the conflicting 'at least once a minute' wording.

Point 7: added one 'Time and memory targets' section (900 s and 100 MB), gave a more careful memory estimate with a 3x row-object allowance, made the benchmark pass criteria match, and added the resume_* columns to the schema as optional.

Point 8: the current-export endpoint now uses finished_at for done exports and explains the 5-minute versus 24-hour link independence; explained that the 429 cap is per server and fleet-wide ceiling scales with server count; made the row_count location an explicit confirm-first assumption and open question 3; defined flag-off behaviour so in-flight exports are not stranded.

Point 1: stated the queue assumption explicitly and added real fencing. Each attempt writes its own object key and own upload, and only the attempt winning the conditional done update records object_key; zombies abort at next heartbeat. Added an overlapping-attempts test and open question 1(a).

Point 2: replaced the three stuck-row cases and updated_at heartbeat with one lease_expires_at column and two shared routines, fail() and reclaim(). Also considered and rejected a sweeper, with the reason.

Point 3: derived all thresholds from one bound. P (per-call timeout) gives H (heartbeat bound), and H plus the max backoff plus pickup gives the 10-minute running lease. The 2-minute lease is justified. The 2-hour queued lease is flagged as the only assumed number.

Point 4: the 30 s timeout is now a parameter P (default 120 s) that the benchmark sets from measured page latency, including the slowest filtered view of the largest report. The benchmark now records per-page and per-part latency.

Point 5: marked the large path's feasibility as gated by the benchmark. Noted that the 450-byte row is derived from the brief and only the 3x overhead is a guess. Specified the resumable fallback's correctness: part boundaries, crash between upload and save, same-part-number replacement verified in the benchmark, 24h expiry versus the under-2-hour retry span, and pagination consistency.

Point 6: removed the per-process 8-slot counter and the 429 response because it did not bound a fleet. The small path is now stateless, bounded by existing API concurrency and the platform per-user rate limit (new open question 4). Justified the buffered response and the bounded, rare stale-count fallback.

Point 7: status endpoint returns 403 on lost access so no filters leak. Retention for done changed to 6 days, with the reason (multipart start can precede finished_at, margin). Download returns 410 past retention. Explained why the in-app button is stricter than the emailed link. Added a test.

Point 8: step 4 is now one flow, insert first, then reclaim on rejection with a single retry, instead of the contradictory pre-check and post-reject handling. Every failure path goes through fail(), which always writes error and finished_at. Stale-count fallback and different-filters cases now return filters/cols and the page tells the user explicitly.
